mainTopic: Combining intentions for פיגול, and רבי יוסי's view on the לבונה of a מנחה
overview: The amud opens by asking why our משנה is needed at all, according to אביי. The גמרא first shows that the rule that two half-olive eating intentions combine into פיגול is already implied by the previous משנה. It then argues that the rule that eating and burning intentions do not combine seems obvious by a קל וחומר from the first clause. It answers that this rule was still needed. The earlier case might fail only because one intention was unusual, but eating and burning are each normal, so we might have thought they combine. Then the chapter כל המנחות closes with הדרן, and a new chapter begins with a משנה. רבי יוסי agrees that a next-day plan for the שיריים or the קומץ makes the מנחה פיגול, but he holds that a plan about the לבונה makes it only פסול. When חכמים compare this to an animal offering, he answers that an animal is one unit, but the לבונה is not part of the מנחה. The גמרא then asks why the משנה says 'רבי יוסי agrees,' and starts explaining that this wording rules out a mistaken reason for his view. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why do we need this משנה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need for our משנה, according to אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this further teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this משנה is needed, since its lessons seem to be known already. This question sets up the next moves, where the גמרא tests possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every משנה must teach something new. If each lesson in our משנה can be found elsewhere, the משנה looks extra. The next steps check each possible lesson one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: This (here: this משנה)
Further, additionally
Why do I need it? (a challenge that something is extra)

phrases.english: Why do I also need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of questioning about why the משנה is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for our משנה, according to אביי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If its lessons can already be learned elsewhere, the משנה has nothing new to teach.

steps.title: The combining of two half-olive eating intentions is already known
steps.stepSummary: One possible lesson is that two eating intentions combine to make פיגול. This is rejected, because the previous משנה already shows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משנה teaches that intending to eat half an olive tomorrow, and again half an olive tomorrow, of food normally eaten, combine, you already learn that from the first part of the last clause of the previous משנה. It says: half an olive outside and half an olive tomorrow is פסול. That implies that half an olive tomorrow and half an olive tomorrow is פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the משנה teaches that two half-olive eating intentions combine into פיגול. It rejects this, because the previous משנה already implies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה rules that 'half outside, half tomorrow' is only פסול, not פיגול, because the two intentions are of different types. The implication is that two halves of the same type, both 'tomorrow', do combine into פיגול. So our משנה is not needed for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Combines (two half-amounts joining into a full amount)
The first part of the last clause
About half an olive-bulk
Unfit (but without the extra penalty of פיגול)
An offering ruined by intent to eat it after its allowed time

phrases.english: If [it teaches the case of intending] to eat and to eat
phrases.notes: He means two separate half-olive intentions to eat the offering tomorrow.

phrases.english: an item that is normally eaten
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word for 'not' in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets leaves it out and reads 'normally eaten.'

phrases.english: it teaches us that they combine
you can learn it from the first part of the last clause
phrases.notes: This refers to the previous משנה, not ours.

phrases.english: as it teaches: half an olive-bulk outside
half an olive-bulk tomorrow, it is unfit
which implies: half an olive-bulk tomorrow
and half an olive-bulk tomorrow is piggul

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לֶאֱכוֹל וְלֶאֱכוֹל דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּמִצְטָרֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible reason for the משנה and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that our משנה is needed to teach that two eating intentions combine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lesson already follows from an inference in the previous משנה.

steps.title: Eating and burning not combining is also already known
steps.stepSummary: A second possible lesson is that intent to eat and intent to burn do not combine. This is rejected, because the first clause of our own משנה implies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משנה is teaching the case of intending to eat and to burn, you can learn that from what is implied in the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the משנה is needed to teach that eating and burning intentions do not combine. It pushes back: the first clause of the משנה already implies this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause speaks of eating 'something normally eaten.' The implication is that intent to eat something not normally eaten does not count toward פיגול. The next step explains how this leads to the eating-and-burning rule.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn on the מזבח
An inference from exact wording
That very thing itself
It teaches us (something new)

phrases.english: If [it teaches the case of intending] to eat and to burn
(that it teaches us that very thing)
phrases.notes: These words in round brackets appear in the printed גמרא, but some versions leave them out.

phrases.english: you can learn it from the inference of the first clause

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible reason for the משנה and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that our משנה is needed to teach that eating and burning don't combine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lesson already follows from an inference in the first clause of the משנה.

steps.title: Explaining the 'how much more so' logic
steps.stepSummary: Two eating intentions don't combine when one is for food not normally eaten. So surely an eating intention and a burning intention don't combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now consider: when he intended to eat something normally eaten and to eat something not normally eaten, you say they don't combine. Do we even need to be told that intending to eat and to burn don't combine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the eating-and-burning rule seems obvious from the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when both intentions are about eating, they fail to combine if one is for something not normally eaten. Eating and burning are two completely different acts, so it seems even more obvious that they would not combine. This is a 'how much more so' argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (introducing a 'consider this' argument)
Something not normally eaten
Is it even needed? (meaning: obviously so)
A 'how much more so' argument

phrases.english: For now consider:
if [intending] to eat and to eat
an item that is not normally eaten
you say they do not combine
is it necessary to teach the case of to eat and to burn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the rejection in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the eating-and-burning case is obvious and so not needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied rule of the first clause: eating something not normally eaten does not combine

steps.title: The eating-and-burning case was still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the eating-and-burning case had to be taught. Otherwise we might have said the earlier case fails only because the eating was unusual.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, the case of eating and burning was needed. It might have entered your mind to say: there, the reason they don't combine is that he was intending something not in its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the eating-and-burning case really is needed. It is not obvious after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'eat plus eat-something-unusual' case, the reason for not combining could be that the second intention was abnormal. But eating and burning are each the normal use of their own items. So without the משנה, we might have thought they do combine.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (to teach)
You might have thought (a mistaken first idea)
Its normal way
He is intending, thinking

steps.whatToRemember: Intent to eat and intent to burn do not combine into פיגול. The משנה must say this outright, because the 'unusual food' case alone would not prove it.
steps.confusionAlert: This step gives only the first half of the contrast: the earlier case fails because the eating was unusual. The next step gives the other half: eating and burning are each normal, so you might have thought they combine.

phrases.english: Yes, [the case of] to eat and to burn
was necessary for him [to teach]
it might have entered your mind to say
that it is there [that they don't combine]
because he intends not in its normal way

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'how much more so' argument of step 4 and defends the need for the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the earlier case had a separate reason, so the 'how much more so' argument fails
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the משנה, one might think eating and burning combine, since both are normal uses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that eating and burning intentions do not combine, even though each is normal.

steps.title: Two normal intentions might seem to combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. In the eating-and-burning case, both intentions are normal, so we might think they combine. The משנה teaches that they don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, where for this half he intends in its normal way, and for this half he intends in its normal way, I might say they should combine. So the משנה teaches us that they don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer from step 5. It explains why the eating-and-burning case needed its own teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, one of the eating intentions was for food not normally eaten, so it was a weak intention. Here, eating the remainder and burning the handful are each done the normal way. So we might have thought they join to a full כזית. The משנה tells us they still don't combine.

keyTerms.meaning: In its normal way (the usual way this part is used)
Has an intention (a thought during the service)
To combine (two half-amounts joining into a full amount)
It teaches us (this is the new point of the text)

steps.whatToRemember: An intention to eat half a כזית and an intention to burn half a כזית do not combine to make פיגול, even though each one is a normal intention.

phrases.english: But here,
phrases.notes: Here means the case in our משנה: half a כזית to eat and half a כזית to burn.

phrases.english: where with this half he intends in its normal way,
and with this half he intends in its normal way,
I might say they should combine,
so it teaches us that they do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא, דִּבְהַאי כִּי אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָמְחַשֵּׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תירוץ begun in step 5 by giving the other side of the contrast.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (a weak abnormal intention versus two normal intentions)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both intentions are normal, they might combine into a full כזית and make פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even two normal intentions of different kinds (eating and burning) do not combine, so the משנה's teaching is needed.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל המנחות
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter כל המנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כל המנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter כל המנחות. It is a closing statement, not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is said at the end of every chapter. It shows that we hope to come back and learn it again. A new chapter starts right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the end-of-chapter formula)
The name of the chapter being closed

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter כל המנחות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter כל המנחות is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: when רבי יוסי agrees, and when he argues
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי agrees that a plan to eat the שיריים or burn the קומץ the next day makes the offering פיגול. A plan to burn the לבונה the next day is argued: רבי יוסי says the offering is only פסול, and חכמים say it is פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a כהן takes the handful from a מנחה planning to eat its remainder or burn its handful tomorrow, רבי יוסי agrees that it is פיגול and one is liable for כרת. If he planned to burn its לבונה tomorrow, רבי יוסי says it is invalid but there is no כרת, and חכמים say it is פיגול and one is liable for כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about wrong-time intentions in a מנחה. It lists cases where רבי יוסי agrees it is פיגול, and one case where he disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating the remainder and burning the handful are the main parts of the מנחה, so all agree a wrong-time plan for them makes פיגול. The לבונה (frankincense) is also burned, but רבי יוסי holds that a plan about it only makes the offering פסול, with no כרת. חכמים say it is full פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes a handful (the כהן's scoop from the מנחה that goes on the מזבח)
The remainder of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים
Frankincense placed on the מנחה and burned on the מזבח
An offering ruined by a plan to eat or burn it at the wrong time; eating it brings כרת
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating פיגול
Invalid, but without the כרת of פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: The קומץ and the לבונה are both burned on the מזבח. Even so, רבי יוסי treats them differently: a plan about the קומץ makes פיגול, but a plan about the לבונה does not.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who takes a handful from the meal offering
planning to eat its remainder
or to burn its handful the next day –
Rabbi Yosei agrees in this case
that it is piggul and one is liable for karet for it.
If he planned to burn its frankincense the next day,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: It is invalid, but there is no karet,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: פִּיגּוּל וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: It is piggul and one is liable for karet for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree a next-day plan for the שיריים or קומץ makes פיגול. For the לבונה, רבי יוסי says the offering is only פסול, while חכמים say it is פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: חכמים compare the מנחה to an animal offering
steps.stepSummary: חכמים ask רבי יוסי how the לבונה case is different from an animal offering, where a plan about the parts burned on the מזבח does make פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: How is this different from an animal offering?
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים challenge רבי יוסי's view on the לבונה. They point to the animal offering as a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an animal offering, a plan to burn the altar portions the next day makes the whole offering פיגול. The לבונה is also burned on the מזבח. So חכמים argue it should work the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal offering
How is it different?

phrases.english: They said to him:
How is this different from an animal offering?
phrases.notes: Some versions have שינה in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets is שנת. Either way it means 'is different.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה שָׁנַת זוֹ מִן הַזֶּבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's ruling about the לבונה in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that a next-day plan for the לבונה does not make פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In an animal offering, a plan about the altar portions makes פיגול. The לבונה is like those altar portions, so it should make פיגול too.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the animal is one unit, but the לבונה is separate
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that an animal's blood, meat, and altar portions are all one unit. The לבונה is not part of the מנחה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: An animal offering's blood, meat, and altar portions are all one, but the לבונה is not part of the מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers חכמים' challenge. He explains why the animal offering is different from the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every part of an animal offering comes from the same animal, so a wrong plan about one part affects the whole offering. The לבונה is a separate substance added on top of the flour. So a plan about it cannot make the מנחה itself פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of an animal offering burned on the מזבח
One (here, one single unit)
A meal (flour) offering

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's reasoning: a wrong-time plan makes פיגול only when it is about part of the same offering. An animal is one unit, but the לבונה is separate from the מנחה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
For an animal offering, its blood, its meat, and its altar portions are one,
but frankincense is not part of the meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: שֶׁהַזֶּבַח דָּמוֹ וּבְשָׂרוֹ וְאֵימוּרָיו אֶחָד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (one unit versus a separate added item)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לבונה is like an animal's altar portions, so a plan about it should make פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: An animal's parts are one unit, but the לבונה is separate from the מנחה, so a plan about it makes the offering only פסול, without כרת.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'רבי יוסי agrees'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the words 'רבי יוסי agrees in this case.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why does the משנה need to teach 'רבי יוסי agrees in this case'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה. It asks why the משנה bothered to write that רבי יוסי agrees about the eating and קומץ cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'agrees' hints that רבי יוסי argues somewhere. The משנה could simply have said 'רבי יוסי says it is פיגול.' The גמרא wants to know why the משנה chose the word 'agrees.'

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
Why do I need it? (asks why words are needed)

phrases.english: גמרא:
Why do I need it to teach
"רבי יוסי agrees in this case"?
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 8, about planning to eat the שיריים or burn the קומץ the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה quoted in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'רבי יוסי agrees' add to the משנה.

steps.title: The words are there because of the לבונה case that follows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'he agrees' because it is leading into the next case. In that case, about burning the לבונה the next day, רבי יוסי says the offering is פסול without כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wants to teach the last case: if he planned to burn its לבונה the next day, רבי יוסי says it is פסול, and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. The words 'he agrees' are connected to the next case in the משנה, the לבונה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the לבונה case, רבי יוסי rules only פסול, not פיגול. That means eating the offering carries no כרת. The גמרא is hinting that the earlier words help us understand this later ruling. The next step explains exactly how.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
It wants to teach
There is no כרת for it (so it is not פיגול)

phrases.english: Because it wants
to teach the last case:
to burn its frankincense the next day,
רבי יוסי says:
it is unfit, but there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 by linking the words to the next case in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'he agrees' are needed because of the following לבונה case, where רבי יוסי says the offering is only פסול.

steps.title: What we might have wrongly thought about רבי יוסי's reason
steps.stepSummary: Without the word 'agrees,' we might think רבי יוסי holds that a plan about half of the מתיר cannot make פיגול. Then even the קומץ case would not be פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי יוסי's reason is that he holds you cannot make פיגול with half of the מתיר. And then even the first case would also not be פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake we might have made without the words 'he agrees.' It lays out this wrong idea, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ and the לבונה together permit the שיריים to be eaten, so each is only half of the מתיר. If רבי יוסי's reason were 'half a מתיר cannot make פיגול,' then a plan about only the קומץ should not make פיגול either. By saying 'he agrees' in the קומץ case, the משנה rules out that reason. His real reason is the one from Step 10: the לבונה is not part of the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken idea the text comes to correct
Make an offering פיגול
Half of the permitting factor; one of two items that together permit the offering
The first part of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is רבי יוסי's real reason. The גמרא brings it only as a mistake the משנה's words come to prevent. His real reason was given in Step 10.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'agrees' tells us that רבי יוסי accepts that a plan about half of the מתיר, the קומץ, can make פיגול. So his ruling in the לבונה case must have a different reason.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the reason of רבי יוסי
is because he holds
one cannot make פיגול with half of the permitting factor,
phrases.notes: The קומץ and the לבונה together permit the שיריים, so a plan about only one of them covers just half.

phrases.english: and then even the first case also [would not be פיגול],
phrases.notes: The first case is the plan to burn the קומץ the next day. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the answer of Step 12 by showing the mistaken reading that the words 'he agrees' prevent.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without the word 'agrees,' one might think רבי יוסי's reason is that half a מתיר cannot make פיגול. That would wrongly extend his ruling to the קומץ case too.
